steps.title: A border region
steps.body: Friuli-Venezia Giulia is Italy's north-eastern corner, bordered by Austria to the north and Slovenia to the east, with the Adriatic to the south. The best vineyards are in the eastern hills: Collio and Colli Orientali del Friuli, on the Slovenian border. The flat Grave plain, in the centre, makes larger volumes.

steps.title: Alpine and Adriatic
steps.body: The climate is shaped by both the Alps, which protect from cold northern winds, and the Adriatic, which brings warm, humid air. The meeting creates a good day and night range and plenty of rain. The hills' soil, ponca, a layered marl and sandstone, drains well and gives mineral, structured whites.

options: A layered marl and sandstone soil
steps.explanation: Ponca gives Friuli's hill whites their structure.

steps.title: A crossroads
steps.body: Friuli has been Roman, Venetian, Austrian and Italian, and its eastern hills continue into Slovenia's Brda. Collio and Brda share grapes, soils and traditions, divided by a border drawn after the Second World War. That crossroads culture shows in its food and in its openness to new and old winemaking.

steps.prompt: Friuli's Collio continues across the border into Slovenia.
steps.explanation: Yes, as Brda, with similar soils and grapes.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Friuli is Italy's north-eastern corner, near Slovenia
The Alps and Adriatic shape its climate
Ponca soils give its hill whites structure
